name: scroll-pageup-moves-viewport
opens_with: A long transcript (200 wrapped lines) renders, then the reader pages up twice while tail-follow is active
notes: P4-1 regression pin (2026-10-09 live audit: the entire keyboard scroll ladder was dead in live sessions). The pageup keys drain before the mock content lands, but the mutation they make - auto_scroll=false + scroll_offset += 10 each - persists while content arrives paused (and the reflow-anchor reconcile grows the offset to keep the reader's chosen position), so the final frame proves the render seam: with the seam broken (pending_resize_anchor returning the per-frame chrome anchor), resize_anchor_scroll overrode user_scroll on every frame and the view stayed pinned to the tail (L199 visible, L020 not). With the one-shot wired, the view parks well above the tail: L020 visible, L199 off-screen. The keys arrive early by harness construction; that is fine because the state, not the key timing, is what the render must honor. THREE presses is where the 2026-10-22 residual defect lived: before iter-1192 the third press landed the reader back at the tail and no press after it moved the view. **This golden pins ONE rung of the ladder (two presses -> ↑20/L014), not the whole climb, and that gap is real but small. The 2026-10-23 note that used to sit here, which said the plain `--dump-screen` path paints a stale frame and therefore that any golden on this path "would pin a frame that lies", was DISPROVEN on 2026-10-23 by re-measuring the deployed release in this corpus's own fixture: the plain path paints the ladder correctly, one step per press (↑40/L101 for zero presses, ↑10/L001 for one, ↑20/L014 for two, ↑40/L101 for four at the ceiling), and ↑20/L014 is exactly what this baseline pins. The earlier reading came from runs that kept pressing past the ceiling, where the offset returns to ↑40 — that is the reader reaching the top of the transcript, not a frame that never settles. Measured both with and without `<esc>` first: identical frames. With the input still focused the PageUps are swallowed at all (0..6 presses each land the identical frame at ↑40/L092, pre-fix and post-fix alike, so that shape discriminates nothing). With `<esc>` releasing focus the ladder IS visible under `--frame-per-event` capture-all — frames 12/13/14 read ↑10/L001, ↑20/L006, ↑30/L049 for four presses — but the plain `--dump-screen` path this golden uses paints the PREVIOUS frame, showing ↑40/L092 for the very same run. Capture-all sets `simulation_one_event_per_frame` so each key gets its own settling frame; the plain path coalesces and the final state never lands (mod.rs: the is_simulating branch). So **any golden written on the plain path would pin a frame that lies about where the reader ended up**, which is why the base assertions stay deliberately tolerant. A golden with real ladder coverage needs the runner to render post-key- settling state — either capture-all or a first-class --dump-screen-equivalent — and that is a harness change, not a scenario change. The authoritative coverage is therefore the unit tests that drive the real key handler and reconcile in the run loop's order: `tui::app::tests::repeated_page_up_climbs_monotonically_and_stops_at_the_real_ceiling` (eight presses), `repeated_wheel_up_climbs_monotonically_and_stops_at_the_real_ceiling` (ten wheel rungs) and `repeated_page_up_walks_upward_monotonically`, all mutation-proven RED without the fix. The fixed-vs-prefix comparison WAS made end to end on 2026-10-23 using capture-all: fixed climbs ↑40, ↑40, ↑10, ↑20, ↑30, ↑40 through six presses; pre-iter-1192 reads ↑40, ↑40, ↑10, ↑20, **↑40**, ↑40 — the fourth press skips ↑30 and snaps to the tail. The defect is real and the fix holds; iter-1200 re-measured it on the deployed release (92642bf0bf85fbc586335a92ed4aa278) under capture-all and got ↑38, ↑38, …, ↑38, ↑40, ↑10, ↑20, ↑30 — monotonic, one step per press. The harness CAN image it on the plain path, so the remaining work is only to add a three-press variant that pins the climb rather than a single rung.
